description: DUMP-kind conformance vectors for @agledger/verify. Each is a directory of five NDJSON files produced by the agledger-api dump-vault tool, then tamper-transformed; verified via verifyDump.

vectors.note: Two record chains, an OIDC-attributed chain, a vault checkpoint, and two org-admin-reads leaves under a signed tree head. Verifies clean.
audit_vault truncated to zero rows. A verifier that reports clean on an empty vault is fail-open; this must surface CHAIN_EMPTY.
All audit_vault rows for the checkpointed record were deleted out of band; the surviving signed checkpoint proves the missing rows.
The signed checkpoint payload_hash no longer matches the audit_vault row at its position — the chain diverged from what was checkpointed.
The denormalised row.payload was rewritten while cose_sign1 still carries the original predicate — binding-integrity failure, not a content judgement.
actor_oidc_synthesized=true but the denormalised actor_oidc_sub was rewritten away from predicate.on_behalf_of.oidc — DBA tamper on a synthesized row.
The signing key was retired one hour before the first entry was written — a retired key produced this entry (the retired-key fail-open fix).
A row signing_key_id was rewritten to an aliased registry entry carrying the same key material. The signature verifies under the alias; only the signature-covered kid (label 4) exposes the rewrite.
vault_signing_keys.algorithm declares ES256 but the key material is Ed25519. The registry lies about its own key; nothing verified against it can be trusted.
The org_admin_reads signed tree head commits to a root that does not match the Merkle root recomputed over its leaves.
Two signed tree heads at the same tree_size carry different roots for the same org — engine fork or signing-key compromise.

Record chain, vault checkpoint, and org-admin-reads tree head all signed under the ES256 vault key (registry row algorithm=ES256). Requires an ES256-capable verifier (wave 2); earlier verifiers fail it CHAIN_UNSUPPORTED_ALGORITHM, fail-closed.
